rows.title: Housing Boom For Whom? Plus, 'Ziwe' Premieres
rows.standfirst: The housing market is booming— but who actually benefits? Sam talks to Jerusalem Demsas, politics and policy fellow for Vox, about what so many are getting wrong about housing. Plus, Sam revisits his 2020 conversation with Ziwe Fumudoh, whose comedy variety show Ziwe premieres on Showtime on May 9. Then, in honor of NPR's 50th anniversary, Sam plays "Who Said That?" with All Things Considered hosts Audie Cornish and Ari Shapiro.

rows.title: Emission Impossible
rows.standfirst: Carbon offsets have become a popular tool to combat climate change. But how effective are they? | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Jobs Friday And The Labor Market Mystery
rows.standfirst: Unemployment is still above 6%, but companies across the US are saying they can't find people to fill their jobs. What's going on?

rows.title: In 1st Big Test, Oversight Board Says Facebook, Not Trump, Is The Problem
rows.standfirst: The first big test of Facebook's Oversight Board reveals the challenges of checking the power and scale of the social media giant.

rows.title: Spring Letdown: Hiring Slows In April, Raising New Challenges For Economy
rows.standfirst: U.S. employers added 266,000 jobs last month, far fewer than analysts had expected. The unemployment rate rose to 6.1%.

rows.title: In A Grief-Filled Year, Brands From Etsy To Pandora Let You Skip Mother's Day Emails
rows.standfirst: The small but growing trend is seen as a welcome acknowledgement of people who are grieving, as well as a sign that email marketing is becoming increasingly personalized and socially conscious.

rows.title: 'Absolute Meltdown': Wall Street's Work Till You Drop Culture Under Attack
rows.standfirst: Burnout in investment banking has been a problem, but the pandemic has made it worse. A handful of firms are responding by offering extra perks and more pay. But more money may not be the answer.

rows.title: Banking On Busy Summer Travel Season, Airlines Add More Flights And New Routes
rows.standfirst: Amid a sudden surge in demand for domestic travel, especially to beach destinations and national parks, decimated airlines are adding service to new markets as they try to inch back to profitability.

rows.title: A Remote Work Revolution Is Underway — But Not For Everyone
rows.standfirst: It's not just tech companies embracing work-from-home for the post-pandemic era. But manufacturers like Ford also have to consider the huge swathes of their workforce that simply can't work remotely.

rows.title: Pepsi's Number Fever
rows.standfirst: Sometimes companies offer sales promotions that are TOO good, ending in livid customers and a disaster for the company.

rows.title: Biden Opens Restaurant Fund With Visit To D.C. Taqueria That's Been On The Brink
rows.standfirst: President Biden encouraged restaurant owners who have been affected by the coronavirus crisis to apply for a grant under the $28.6 billion program.

rows.title: 'So Exciting To Be Working Again': Americans Are Going Out, Boosting Jobs
rows.standfirst: Newly vaccinated Americans are spending more freely on restaurants, travel and live entertainment. That should give a boost to pandemic-scarred service industries.

rows.title: Why Facebook's Decision On Trump Could Be 'Make Or Break' For His Political Future
rows.standfirst: Facebook's Oversight Board sent the decision of whether to let the former president back on the platform back to the company itself, and it's a critical one for Trump's political future.

rows.title: Google Adapts To Long-Term Telework, Offers Employees Hybrid Workweek
rows.standfirst: More than a year into telework, the tech giant has said about 60% of its employees will work remotely two days a week. Twenty percent will work from home permanently.

rows.title: The VITA(L) Role Of Free Tax Prep
rows.standfirst: The IRS helps millions of people do their taxes FOR FREE every year. But, as with many things in the past year, covid has made this a little more complicated.

rows.title: Walmart Drops Mask Mandate Following New CDC Guidelines
rows.standfirst: Customers don't have to wear masks, effective immediately. Starting Tuesday, fully vaccinated employees don't either. Everyone's on an honor system and won't have to provide proof.

rows.title: Brood X Economy: Indicators Of The Week
rows.standfirst: The Brood X cicadas are finally back this summer, but what was life like 17 years ago when they first went underground?

rows.title: Fuel Shortages Should Ease Over Coming Days As Colonial Fully Restarts Pipelines
rows.standfirst: The supply chain for fuels like gasoline will take several days to return to normal after Colonial restarted a critical pipeline that was shut down this month.

rows.title: Americans Dialed Back On Retail Therapy — And Spent More Eating Their Feelings
rows.standfirst: Retail sales were flat in April from a month earlier as Americans spent less on things such as clothes or sporting goods but increased their spending at bars and restaurants.

rows.title: More Cities Are Handing People Cash With No Strings Attached. Here's Why
rows.standfirst: Nearly two dozen American cities have signed on to pilot programs that offer basic incomes to low-income residents.

rows.title: Just 12 People Are Behind Most Vaccine Hoaxes On Social Media, Research Shows
rows.standfirst: The majority of false claims about COVID-19 vaccines on social media trace back to just a handful of influential figures. So why don't the companies just shut them down?

rows.title: How Do You Get People To Get A Vaccine?
rows.standfirst: What's the best way to persuade people to get a vaccine? A new study from the University of Pennsylvania may have the answer.

rows.title: Biden Says 'Help Is On The Way' As Colonial Pipeline Restarts Flow Of Fuel
rows.standfirst: The president cautions it will be several days before gas flow is fully restored. He urges consumers not to panic and hoard gasoline while warning gas stations not to gouge prices.

rows.title: How To Stop Ransomware Attacks? 1 Proposal Would Prohibit Victims From Paying Up
rows.standfirst: The attack on Colonial Pipeline has focused new attention on a potentially radical proposal to stem the growing threat posed by ransomware: making it illegal for victims to pay their attackers.

rows.title: FAA OKs Fix For Electrical Issue That Grounded Some Boeing 737 Max Jets
rows.standfirst: The issue temporarily took more than 100 newly built 737 Max planes out of service last month, but is unrelated to the flight control system problem blamed for two fatal crashes.

rows.title: Crash, Arrest Draw More Scrutiny Of Tesla Autopilot System
rows.standfirst: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration faces pressure to take action on Tesla's partially automated driving system, which has been involved in at least three U.S. deaths.

rows.title: Hot Cheetos
rows.standfirst: A janitor walks out of a chip factory with a bag of dustless Cheetos and changes the global snack game forever. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Never Mind: Elon Musk Says Tesla Won't Accept Bitcoin For Car Purchases Any More
rows.standfirst: Tesla's CEO explained on Twitter that the reversal on accepting Bitcoin was prompted by concerns about the "rapidly increasing use of fossil fuels" to mine the cryptocurrency.

rows.title: In Wake Of Pipeline Hack, Biden Signs Executive Order On Cybersecurity
rows.standfirst: The order follows a ransomware attack on a company that operates a pipeline that provides nearly half of the gasoline and jet fuel for the East Coast.

rows.title: Stewie Gets Her Own Sneaks: WNBA Star Pens First Deal In A Decade
rows.standfirst: Breanna Stewart's new sneaker deal with Puma includes the first signature shoe for a WNBA player in a decade. ESPN's Nick DePaula tells NPR's Mary Louise Kelly what it means for the industry.

rows.title: The 'Charlie Bit My Finger' Viral Video Will Leave YouTube And Sell As NFT
rows.standfirst: The 2007 home video raised the bar for "going viral." Now, the famous brothers are deleting the video from YouTube on May 23 to auction it off as a nonfungible token.

rows.title: Labor Market Mysteries; Plus, Signs Of Life
rows.standfirst: The U.S. unemployment rate is still high... so why are we in a labor shortage? Sam chats with Stacey Vanek Smith, host of NPR's The Indicator , and Cardiff Garcia, former co-host of The Indicator , about the American job market and why businesses are having such a hard time hiring. Then, as vaccines have become more widely available and pandemic restrictions lift across the country, people are wandering back out into the world, having experiences they haven't had in over a year. We drop in on a few of these: a dance party, a first date, a game with friends — the small pleasures folks have missed that now feel monumental.

rows.title: Big Government Cheese (CLASSIC)
rows.standfirst: That time the U.S. government accidentally created a cheese surplus so large it had to be stored in a ginormous cave. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: As Apple's Tim Cook Testifies, The Judge Creates The Day's Most Dramatic Moment
rows.standfirst: CEO Tim Cook defended Apple on the witness stand on Friday in a trial playing out in Oakland, Calif. Epic Games, which is suing Apple, accuses it of being an illegal monopoly.

rows.title: Dogecoin, Retail And The Cafe Table Indicator
rows.standfirst: For this edition of Indicators of the Week, we hear from economists Kate Waldock and Ben Ho about what they're looking at to signal the health of the economy: the strength of retail and Dogecoin.

rows.title: A Team Of Mostly Women Races To Make History At The Indianapolis 500
rows.standfirst: Over the years, only nine women have driven in the marquee event. But this year, one of 35 teams competing to qualify — including the driver, owner and crew — is made up mostly of women.

rows.title: 'Vulture' Fund Alden Global, Known For Slashing Newsrooms, Buys Tribune Papers
rows.standfirst: Hedge fund Alden Global Capital, known for making deep newsroom cuts, won approval to acquire Tribune Publishing, which includes the Chicago Tribune , The Baltimore Sun and New York Daily News .

rows.title: Amazon Shuts Down A Construction Site In Connecticut After A 7th Noose Is Found
rows.standfirst: The latest noose was found hanging from a beam during a lunch break on Wednesday. Amazon says a $100,000 reward is being offered for information leading to the identity of the culprits.

rows.title: Restaurants Are Welcoming Back Diners, But Say Mask Rules Have Them Relying On Trust
rows.standfirst: The National Restaurant Association is recommending to its members that employees continue to wear masks until the government clarifies how the guidance applies to a requirement to keep workers safe.

rows.title: A Black Woman Says She Had To Hide Her Race To Get A Fair Home Appraisal
rows.standfirst: Two low home appraisals spurred a Black woman in Indianapolis to administer her own fair housing test. The result led her to file a complaint alleging housing discrimination.

rows.title: Apple CEO Tim Cook Is Taking The Witness Stand Friday. Here's Why It's A Big Deal
rows.standfirst: CEO Tim Cook will defend his company against accusations from Epic Games that Apple has an illegal monopoly. The trial has focused on a 30% commission on most purchases made in the Apple App Store.

rows.title: Biden Wants To Measure How Climate Change Impacts America's Finances
rows.standfirst: President Biden signed an executive order Thursday that aims to safeguard families, businesses, and the government from the financial fallout of a changing climate.

rows.title: America's Best-Selling Truck Goes Electric
rows.standfirst: The Ford Lightning is the first electric F-150 pickup truck, and it could be a historical tipping point for the US auto industry. The only problem? Selling it to old-school drivers.

rows.title: Bitcoin Is Plunging. What To Know About The Wild Ride In Cryptocurrencies
rows.standfirst: Weeks after setting a record high, the price for Bitcoin has fallen dramatically along with other cryptocurrencies over factors ranging from inflation to, yes, Elon Musk.

rows.title: Ford Says Electric F-150 Will Start Under $40,000. It Can Also Power Your Home
rows.standfirst: The F-150 Lightning, the electric version of Ford's bestselling pickup, has a base price of just under $40,000 and can be set up as a backup energy source for your home if the power goes out.

rows.title: How Tulsa Race Massacre Shaped Today's Most Successful Black CEOs
rows.standfirst: Ariel Investments CEO John Rogers, TIAA CEO Thasunda Duckett, and former American Express CEO Kenneth Chenault reflect on what the Tulsa events a century ago has meant to them.

rows.title: Why Democrats Are Angry At Wall Street
rows.standfirst: Big banks are facing a new reality in Washington: Democrats control all levers of power and they are not shy about their intentions to ratchet up pressure on the sector.

rows.title: Startup Helps Those Affected By Gangs And Gun Violence Find A Way Out
rows.standfirst: One small startup in Portland, Ore., is helping place former gang members and others involved in gun violence into well-paying green energy jobs.

rows.title: The Buffet Can Stay: What The Future Of The Cruise Line Industry Looks Like
rows.standfirst: The first post-pandemic cruise from a U.S. port will embark next month. Despite CDC measures, the go-ahead puts wind in the sails of cruise lines, which have high hopes for an in-demand industry.

rows.title: Think Inflation Is Bad Now? Let's Take A Step Back To The 1970s
rows.standfirst: Prices are jumping as the economy rebounds from the pandemic, but the Biden Administration and the Federal Reserve say a return to 1970s-style inflation is unlikely.

rows.title: One Hack to Fool Them All
rows.standfirst: How a single hack pried open the networks of giant corporations and the U.S. government itself. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Unpacking President Biden's Big Budget
rows.standfirst: President Biden unveiled a massive budget proposal on Friday. We discuss the hefty price tag and ask two economists to weigh in on his plan.

rows.title: The FAA Has Seen A 'Significantly Higher' Number Of Unruly Passenger Reports In 2021
rows.standfirst: After a flight attendant lost two teeth during an attack by a customer, Southwest Airlines decided to delay its return to serving passengers alcohol.

rows.title: What We Know About The Apparent Russian Hack Exploiting A U.S. Aid Agency
rows.standfirst: Screenshots of the malicious email show that it purports to be a special alert from the government. "Donald Trump has published new documents on election fraud," the message declares.

rows.title: Live Music Is Back, But You Might Still Have To Wait On That Arena Show
rows.standfirst: Live music giants AEG Presents and Live Nation say they've got a surplus of acts wanting to play as soon as possible.

rows.title: Employers Can (Mostly) Require Vaccines For Workers Returning To The Office
rows.standfirst: Guidance from the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission says employers can legally require workers to get a COVID-19 vaccine before returning to the office. But workers can claim exceptions.

rows.title: Homebuyers Squeezed As Western States See Prices Double Or More In Last Decade
rows.standfirst: The pandemic has made the housing market even tighter in the mountain West, where first-time buyers are trying to decide whether this is just the future or a bubble headed eventually for a bust.

rows.title: The Year We Learned To Cook Seafood At Home, And Sent Prices Soaring
rows.standfirst: A lot of Americans learned to shuck oysters and cook fish at home during the pandemic. Now that restaurants are getting back to normal, there's a supply crunch.

rows.title: The Week That Shook Big Oil
rows.standfirst: A set of events shook the oil world this week: A tiny shareholder won a battle with Exxon, investors put pressure on Chevron and a Dutch court ordered Shell to slash emissions.

rows.title: Harris Pushes Companies To Invest In Guatemala, Honduras And El Salvador
rows.standfirst: Vice President Harris met with a dozen companies and NGOs that have agreed to invest in the Northern Triangle countries. It's part of an effort to address the root causes of migration to the U.S.
